title: C3NN-SBI: Learning Hierarchies of $N$-Point Statistics from Cosmological Fields with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
summary: Cosmological analyses are moving past the well understood 2-point statistics to extract more information from cosmological fields. A natural step in extending inference pipelines to other summary statistics is to include higher order N-point correlation functions (NPCFs), which are computationally expensive and difficult to model. At the same time it is unclear how many NPCFs one would have to include to reasonably exhaust the cosmological information in the observable fields. An efficient alternative is given by learned and optimized summary statistics, largely driven by overparametrization through neural networks. This, however, largely abandons our physical intuition on the NPCF formalism and information extraction becomes opaque to the practitioner. We design a simulation-based inference pipeline, that not only benefits from the efficiency of machine learned summaries through optimization, but also holds on to the NPCF program. We employ the heavily constrained Cosmological Correlator Convolutional Neural Network (C3NN) which extracts summary statistics that can be directly linked to a given order NPCF. We present an application of our framework to simulated lensing convergence maps and study the information content of our learned summary at various orders in NPCFs for this idealized example. We view our approach as an exciting new avenue for physics-informed simulation-based inference.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a simulation-based inference method using C3NN to extract physically interpretable, machine-learned summary statistics aligned with higher order N-point correlation functions, improving cosmological analyses beyond standard 2-point approaches.
AI.motivation: To extend cosmological inference beyond 2-point statistics and efficiently extract more information from cosmological fields using higher order N-point correlation functions (NPCFs) while retaining physical interpretability.
AI.method: Developed a simulation-based inference pipeline using the Cosmological Correlator Convolutional Neural Network (C3NN) that learns optimized summary statistics linked directly to specific orders of NPCFs, applied to simulated lensing convergence maps.
AI.result: Demonstrated that the C3NN framework can efficiently extract informative summary statistics corresponding to various NPCF orders, enabling physics-informed and interpretable inference from cosmological data.
AI.conclusion: The approach provides a promising, interpretable, and efficient alternative to traditional NPCF computations by integrating machine learning with physical modeling, helping to better capture cosmological information beyond traditional 2-point statistics.

title: The Sign-Switching of the Cosmological Constant
comment: 21 pages, 5 figures. Contribution to the proceedings of the Corfu Summer Institute 2025 "School and Workshops on Elementary Particle Physics and Gravity" (CORFU2025) 2 - 8 September, 2025 Corfu, Greece
summary: We propose and investigate a class of dynamical dark energy models in which the cosmological constant evolves from negative values in the early Universe to a positive value at low redshifts. This framework includes a generalised ladder-step evolution, as well as smooth-transition scenarios, providing a unified description of sign-changing cosmological constants. We analyse the theoretical construction and background dynamics of these models using cosmographic diagnostics. Extending this study to the linear perturbation regime, we solve the perturbation equations from the radiation-dominated era with adiabatic initial conditions. We examine the evolution of the matter density contrast, gravitational potential, and the $fσ_8$ observable. Our results are compared against the standard $Λ$CDM model and confronted with current observational data, illustrating the phenomenological viability of sign-changing dark energy models and revealing distinctive imprints on cosmic structure formation arising from the transition of the cosmological constant.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes and studies models where the cosmological constant evolves from negative to positive values, analyzes their theoretical and perturbation dynamics, and shows they fit observations while imprinting unique features on cosmic structure formation.
AI.motivation: To explore dynamical dark energy models where the cosmological constant changes sign from negative in the early Universe to positive at late times, addressing limitations of a fixed cosmological constant and its impact on cosmic evolution.
AI.method: Developed models with generalized ladder-step and smooth-transition evolutions of the cosmological constant; analyzed background dynamics using cosmographic diagnostics; solved linear perturbation equations from radiation era with adiabatic initial conditions; studied matter density contrast, gravitational potential, and fσ8 observable.
AI.result: Demonstrated that sign-changing cosmological constant models are phenomenologically viable and produce distinctive signatures in cosmic structure formation compared to standard ΛCDM; models align with current observational data.
AI.conclusion: Sign-changing dynamical dark energy models provide a unified framework extending beyond ΛCDM, with observable differences in structure formation that could be tested with cosmological data.

title: Testing the cosmic distance-duality relation with localized fast radio bursts: a cosmological model-independent study
summary: We test the Etherington cosmic distance-duality relation (CDDR), by comparing Type Ia supernova (SNIa) luminosity-distance information from the Pantheon+ compilation with an angular-diameter-distance reconstructed from localized Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs). The core of our methodology is a data-driven reconstruction from FRBs using artificial neural networks (ANNs): we infer a smooth mean extragalactic dispersion-measure relation and use its redshift derivative to recover $H(z)$ and hence $D_\mathrm{A}^{\rm FRB}(z)$ without assuming a parametric form for the expansion history. Possible deviations from CDDR are parameterized through three one-parameter models of $η(z)\equiv D_\mathrm{L}/[(1+z)^2D_\mathrm{A}]$. We implement two complementary likelihoods: (i) a direct approach using individual SNIa with the full Pantheon+ covariance, and (ii) a machine-learning approach in which we reconstruct the SN Hubble diagram on the FRB redshift grid, propagating SN and FRB uncertainties into non-diagonal covariance matrices via Monte Carlo and bootstrap realizations. Within the FRB reconstruction, we anchor the mean extragalactic dispersion measure at $z=0$, which yields a data-driven constraint on the average host/near-source contribution $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm host}=128.8\pm 34.1\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ ($3σ$ of statistical confidence). We find that both likelihood implementations give consistent posteriors and no statistically significant evidence for departures from CDDR at the current precision.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a model-independent test of the cosmic distance-duality relation using neural network reconstruction of angular-diameter distances from FRB dispersion measures and luminosity distances from Type Ia supernovae, finding no significant deviations and providing a data-driven constraint on host dispersion measures.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to test the Etherington cosmic distance-duality relation by comparing independent and complementary distance measurements obtained from Type Ia supernovae luminosity distances and angular-diameter distances reconstructed from localized FRBs, thereby providing a model-independent and data-driven test of CDDR.
AI.method: The method involves a data-driven reconstruction using artificial neural networks (ANNs) on Fast Radio Burst (FRB) data to infer a smooth extragalactic dispersion-measure relation and its redshift derivative, which recovers $H(z)$ and angular-diameter distance $D_A^{FRB}(z)$ without assuming a parametric expansion history. Two likelihood approaches were used to test CDDR: (i) a direct approach with individual Type Ia supernova data and (ii) a machine-learning approach reconstructing the supernova Hubble diagram on the FRB redshift grid, propagating uncertainties via Monte Carlo and bootstrap sampling.
AI.result: The analysis produced a constraint on the average host/near-source dispersion measure contribution $	{DM}_{host}=128.8\pm 34.1\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ at $3\sigma$ confidence, and both likelihood methods yielded consistent posterior distributions with no significant deviations from CDDR observed.
AI.conclusion: No statistically significant evidence for departures from the Etherington cosmic distance-duality relation (CDDR) was found at the current observational precision.

title: Investigating IceCube Neutrino Alerts with the HAWC $γ$-Ray Observatory
summary: Neutrino emission from astrophysical sources has long been considered a signature of cosmic-ray acceleration. The IceCube neutrino observatory has observed a diffuse flux of TeV-PeV neutrinos, but very few confirmed sources have emerged. With the recent publication of IceCube Event Catalog (IceCat-1), IceCube has released a list of the most promising astrophysical neutrino events since May 2011. Using the archival data from the High Altitude Water Cherenkov (HAWC) $γ$-ray observatory, we perform a coincidence search for gamma rays and neutrinos using a Bayesian Block algorithm with the public IceCube alerts from IceCat-1, along with additional alerts issued later. In this work, we consider 368 alerts, up to July 8, 2025, that are within HAWC's field of view. We observe approximately a 5\% coincident detection rate, which is consistent with expectations from background. Two of these detections contain the Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) Markarian 421 and Markarian 501. We discuss the likelihood that the neutrino/$γ$-ray coincidences are false positives and a brief overview of the results.

AI.tldr: This paper reports a search for coincident gamma-ray and neutrino signals using IceCube neutrino alerts and HAWC gamma-ray data, finding a 5% coincidence rate consistent with background, including two detections linked to notable AGNs.
AI.motivation: To identify astrophysical sources of cosmic-ray acceleration by detecting coincident neutrino and gamma-ray emissions, leveraging the newly published IceCube event catalog and existing gamma-ray observatory data.
AI.method: A coincidence search was conducted using archival HAWC gamma-ray data and IceCube neutrino alert data (IceCat-1 and subsequent alerts), employing a Bayesian Block algorithm to identify temporal coincidences within HAWC's field of view.
AI.result: Approximately 5% of the 368 neutrino alerts coincided with gamma-ray detections, corresponding to expected background levels; two coincident events involved AGNs Markarian 421 and Markarian 501, though no unambiguous source identifications were established.
AI.conclusion: The study found a 5% coincident detection rate of gamma rays and neutrinos, consistent with background expectations, and identified two detections linked to the AGNs Markarian 421 and Markarian 501, without definitive confirmation of true astrophysical sources.

title: X-ray Spectral-Timing Properties of Tidal Disruption Events
summary: We perform the first systematic study of the minute-to-hours-timescale stochastic variability observed in the X-ray luminosity of tidal disruption events (TDEs) using XMM-Newton data and Fourier analysis methods. We measure the spectral properties, power spectral densities (PSDs), fractional variability amplitudes, and energy dependence of the variability for 18 TDEs spanning 54 observations, of which 27 occur in thermal disk-dominated states and 27 show a nonthermal hard X-ray corona. Compared to pure thermal sources, we find TDEs with coronae are more X-ray variable and show steeper PSDs indicating longer correlation timescales. This state-transition behavior is qualitatively similar to X-ray binaries, which show higher fractional variability in the hard state than in the soft state. However, newborn TDE coronae show systematically flatter PSDs and softer energy spectra than their long-lived AGN counterparts. We also show that the variability amplitude of thermal TDEs increases with photon energy, consistent with variations sourced by local temperature fluctuations and exponentially enhanced in the Wien tail. Our work demonstrates that combining spectral and timing properties of X-ray TDEs can probe the microphysics of newly formed accretion flows around supermassive black holes, and that the coronae formed in TDEs fundamentally differ from those in AGN.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes X-ray variability of 18 tidal disruption events, finding that coronae-bearing TDEs show greater variability and different spectral-timing properties than thermal TDEs and AGN, providing insight into accretion flow physics around supermassive black holes.
AI.motivation: To understand the stochastic X-ray variability behavior of tidal disruption events and compare the properties of thermal versus nonthermal states, and how these newly formed accretion flows differ from those in active galactic nuclei.
AI.method: Systematic analysis of minute-to-hours timescale X-ray variability using XMM-Newton data and Fourier methods to measure spectral properties, power spectral densities, fractional variability, and energy dependence in 18 TDEs over 54 observations.
AI.result: TDEs with coronae exhibit higher X-ray variability and steeper PSDs than thermal TDEs; newborn TDE coronae have flatter PSDs and softer spectra compared to AGN coronae; variability amplitude in thermal TDEs increases with photon energy, consistent with temperature fluctuation models.
AI.conclusion: X-ray variability studies reveal that TDEs with hard X-ray coronae are more variable and possess longer correlation timescales compared to thermal disk-dominated TDEs, similar to state transitions in X-ray binaries, but with distinctive spectral properties from AGN coronae.

title: Cosmic voids evolution in modified gravity via hydrodynamics
summary: We present a hydrodynamical description of spherical void evolution in modified gravity (MG), extending the standard General Relativity (GR) and dynamical dark energy treatment by encoding gravity modifications into effective couplings that enter the Euler and Poisson equations. This yields a compact non-linear evolution equation for the Eulerian density contrast, controlled by a time- and density-dependent effective gravitational strength, and provides a direct map between model functions and void observables. We apply the framework to the luminal Galileon class of models, where derivative self-interactions generate Vainshtein screening and might lead to a breakdown of the physical branch in sufficiently underdense regions. Exploiting this feature, we apply the void-informed viability requirement that translates into bounds on the theory parameter space and, equivalently, on the minimum attainable void depth as a function of redshift. For viable parameters of a concrete model, we quantify the impact of MG on isolated void evolution, the Lagrangian to Eulerian mapping, and the shell-crossing threshold. Relative to GR, we find a clear hierarchy of MG effects, with ${\cal O}(10\%)$ modifications in the gravitational couplings, percent-level shifts in the void density evolution, and sub-percent deviations in both the mapping and the shell-crossing thresholds. Moreover, within the adopted parametrization, we show analytically that voids always lie in an unscreened regime on the physical branch. Overall, the formalism provides a self-consistent route to predict void dynamics and consistency constraints in a broad class of MG models.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic model extending GR by encoding modified gravity effects into effective couplings governing void evolution. Applied to luminal Galileon models, it constrains parameter space via void properties and quantifies MG impacts, revealing moderate modifications in gravitational couplings and density evolution, with voids consistently unscreened.
AI.motivation: To develop a comprehensive and compact theoretical framework enabling the prediction of void dynamics within modified gravity scenarios, facilitating a direct connection between model parameters and observables. The work aims to exploit voids as probes to place viability constraints on modified gravity theories, particularly where screening phenomena and branch breakdown may occur.
AI.method: The authors extended the standard GR and dynamical dark energy hydrodynamical approach by incorporating modifications into effective gravitational couplings affecting the Euler and Poisson equations. They derived a non-linear evolution equation for Eulerian density contrast dependent on time and density. This method was applied specifically to luminal Galileon models with derivative self-interactions generating Vainshtein screening, analyzing void evolution, mapping, and shell-crossing thresholds.
AI.result: The study finds that modified gravity introduces order ~10% changes in gravitational couplings affecting void evolution, with percent-level changes in void density and smaller sub-percent modifications to mapping functions and shell-crossing thresholds. It establishes bounds on theory parameters from void viability, shows voids reside in unscreened regimes on the physical branch, and clarifies the hierarchical impact of MG effects relative to GR.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that the hydrodynamical framework provides a self-consistent, compact, and effective method to describe spherical void evolution in modified gravity models, yielding observable signatures that can constrain the theory parameter space. It also finds that voids stay in an unscreened regime for the physical branch in the luminal Galileon model and quantifies the magnitude of modified gravity effects compared to General Relativity.

title: WFST Supernovae in the First Year: I. Statistical Study of 16 Early-phase Type Ia Supernovae from the Pilot Survey
comment: 23 pages, 14 figures, 3 tables, revised version submitted to RAA
summary: In this paper we present 16 early-phase type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) discovered during the pilot survey of the 2.5-meter Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST-PS) from March 4 to July 10, 2024, including three SNe Ia with early-excess emission features (EExSNe Ia). The discovery magnitude of the 16 WFST-PS early-phase SNe is at least 3 mag fainter than their peak brightness. A large scatter of color indices is found in approximately the first 10 days of supernova explosions, indicating diverse photometric behaviors in the early phase. Three EExSNe Ia show relatively brighter peak luminosities and longer rise time compared to those of non-EExSNe Ia. The results indicate that current theoretical models require further refinement to fully capture the early photometric evolution of SNe Ia. Based on the initial high-cadence ugr-band data from the WFST-PS survey, we emphasize that early near-ultraviolet (NUV) observations are indispensable for placing tight constraints on the explosion mechanisms and progenitor systems of SNe Ia.

AI.tldr: This study reports 16 early-phase type Ia supernovae discovered by WFST-PS, highlighting diverse early light curve behaviors and the importance of early near-UV data to better understand explosion mechanisms and progenitors.
AI.motivation: To improve understanding of the early photometric behaviors and explosion mechanisms of type Ia supernovae by capturing data closer to the onset of explosion, especially to investigate early-excess emission features.
AI.method: A pilot survey using the 2.5-meter Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST-PS) was conducted between March and July 2024, discovering 16 early-phase type Ia supernovae, with detailed high-cadence ugr-band photometric observations, including analysis of color indices and rise times.
AI.result: 16 early-phase SNe Ia were discovered with discovery magnitudes significantly fainter than peak brightness; notable color index scatter was observed in the first 10 days; three early-excess emission SNe Ia displayed brighter peak luminosities and longer rise times; emphasizing the necessity of early near-ultraviolet observations for constraining explosion models and progenitor systems.
AI.conclusion: Current theoretical models are insufficient to fully describe the early photometric evolution of type Ia supernovae, as revealed by diverse early-phase behaviors and distinctive features in early-excess emission SNe Ia.

title: WFST Supernovae in the First Year: II. SN 2024aedt: Systematical Study of a Transitional Type Ia Supernova
comment: 24 pages, 20 figures, 3 tables, revised version submitted to ApJ
summary: We present comprehensive photometric and spectroscopic observations of a transitional type Ia SN 2024aedt, discovered by the 2.5-meter Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST) within one day of the explosion. Its light curve is characterized by a peak absolute magnitude of $M_B = -18.49 \pm 0.03$ mag and a decline rate of $Δm_{15}(B) = 1.53 \pm 0.36$ mag, placing the object on the $Δm_{15}(B)$--$M_B$ diagram in the transition region between normal and subluminous SNe Ia. Furthermore, the early-color evolution and host galaxy environment of SN 2024aedt underscore its transitional nature, sharing properties with both normal and 91bg-like SNe Ia. Light-curve modeling with MOSFiT yields a synthesized $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ mass of $0.414 \pm 0.042\,M_{\odot}$ and a total ejecta mass of $0.548 \pm 0.108\,M_{\odot}$. A comparison with theoretical models suggests that the evolutionary trend can be broadly explained by both delayed-detonation (DDT) and double-detonation (DDet) scenarios while possible early-excess emissions predicted by DDet cannot be identified given the limited detections soon after the SN explosion. Although the overall spectral evolution of SN 2024aedt is similar to that of other transitional SNe Ia, the spectroscopic comparison reveals diversity in the early-phase blue-end features, which becomes more homogeneous at later phases. The result indicates the importance of early-time observations in understanding the origin of SN Ia diversity.

AI.tldr: We observed and modeled the transitional SN Ia 2024aedt, demonstrating its intermediate properties and ejecta characteristics consistent with multiple explosion theories, and showed early spectral diversity crucial for understanding SN Ia progenitors and diversity.
AI.motivation: To characterize and understand the nature and diversity of transitional Type Ia supernovae, which lie between normal and subluminous categories, and to explore their progenitor and explosion scenarios.
AI.method: Comprehensive photometric and spectroscopic observations were made starting within one day post-explosion, light-curve modeling with MOSFiT was used to estimate nickel and ejecta masses, and comparisons with theoretical DDT and DDet models were conducted.
AI.result: SN 2024aedt lies in the transitional region on the decline rate versus peak magnitude diagram, synthesizes about 0.414 solar masses of 56Ni with a total ejecta mass of ~0.548 solar masses, and its spectral evolution aligns broadly with both delayed-detonation and double-detonation models; early-phase spectral diversity highlights the role of early observations in SN Ia diversity studies.
AI.conclusion: SN 2024aedt is a transitional Type Ia supernova exhibiting properties between normal and subluminous SNe Ia, confirmed through photometric, spectroscopic observations, and light-curve modeling. Early-time features show diversity, emphasizing the need for early observations to understand SN Ia origins.

title: Modeling of Relativistic Plasmas with a Conservative Discontinuous Galerkin Method
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, submitted to Nature Computational Science
summary: We present a new method for solving the relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell system of equations, applicable to a wide range of extreme high-energy-density astrophysical and laboratory environments. The method directly discretizes the kinetic equation on a high-dimensional phase-space grid using a discontinuous Galerkin finite element approach, yielding a high-order, conservative numerical scheme that is free from the Poisson noise inherent to traditional Monte-Carlo methods. A novel and flexible velocity-space mapping technique enables the efficient treatment of the wide range of energy scales characteristic of relativistic plasmas, including QED pair-production discharges, instabilities in strongly magnetized plasmas surrounding neutron stars, and relativistic magnetic reconnection. Our noise-free approach is capable of providing unique insight into plasma dynamics, enabling detailed analysis of electromagnetic emission and fine-scale phase-space structure.

AI.tldr: A novel discontinuous Galerkin-based numerical method is developed for simulating relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell plasmas with high accuracy and no noise, applicable to diverse high-energy plasma environments.
AI.motivation: To overcome limitations of traditional Monte-Carlo methods, especially Poisson noise, and to accurately simulate complex, high-energy plasma environments occurring in astrophysics and laboratory settings.
AI.method: A high-dimensional phase-space grid is discretized directly using a discontinuous Galerkin finite element approach, coupled with a novel velocity-space mapping technique to efficiently handle wide energy ranges in relativistic plasmas.
AI.result: The method successfully handles multiple physical scenarios including QED pair-production discharges, magnetized plasma instabilities near neutron stars, and relativistic magnetic reconnection, providing detailed insights into plasma dynamics and electromagnetic emission without noise artifacts.
AI.conclusion: The presented method offers a robust, noise-free, high-order numerical scheme for solving the relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell system, enabling advanced analysis of complex plasma phenomena across extreme energy scales.

title: The spectral state transition of Mkn 590, a potential link between AGNs and X-ray binaries?
summary: The Seyfert galaxy Markarian 590 offers a rare glimpse into the dynamic life cycle of black hole accretion, captured across multiple wavelengths from the years 1975 to 2025. Using the decade-long multi-band observations from the Swift observatory, we capture a clear spectral state transition analogous to those seen in X-ray binaries but seldom observed in a single AGN. We track a complete AGN state transition in real time, as the source evolves from a faint, hard X-ray state to a bright, UV- and soft X-ray dominated phase. The X-ray loudness parameter $α_{ox}$ follows a pronounced 'V'-shaped dependence on Eddington ratio $λ_{Edd}$, with a break at $λ_{Edd}$ = 0.021 +/- 0.008, coinciding with thresholds identified in population studies of changing-look quasars and X-ray binaries. Across this transition, Mkn 590 evolves through distinct accretion regimes in the Hardness Intensity Diagrams (HID): faint, flaring, transitional, and bright, on a timescale of $\sim$10 years, which is well below classical viscous timescales for a geometrically thin disk but in agreement with the propagation of thermal wavefronts in the inner disk. When placed on the Fundamental Plane of black hole activity, the source broadly follows the expected radio/X-ray mass scaling, though with a 70% flatter slope, pointing towards a persistent coronal-jet coupling even in radiatively efficient states. Together, our results establish Mkn 590 as a rare, time-resolved case of AGN state transitions and offer compelling evidence for scale-invariant accretion physics across the black hole mass spectrum.

AI.tldr: Markarian 590 was monitored over decades, revealing a rare AGN spectral state transition analogous to X-ray binaries, confirming universal accretion physics and persistent jet coupling across black hole masses.
AI.motivation: To capture and analyze an active galactic nucleus (AGN) undergoing a full spectral state transition in real time, which are rarely observed in a single AGN, to understand the underlying accretion physics and draw parallels with X-ray binaries and changing-look quasars.
AI.method: The study utilized multiwavelength observational data spanning 1975-2025, particularly decade-long multi-band monitoring from the Swift observatory, analyzing spectral states, X-ray loudness (α_ox), Eddington ratios, Hardness Intensity Diagrams, and positioning on the Fundamental Plane for black hole activity.
AI.result: The AGN transitions from a faint, hard X-ray state to a bright UV- and soft X-ray state over ~10 years, with a pronounced V-shaped α_ox dependence on Eddington ratio and distinct accretion regimes noted in Hardness Intensity Diagrams; the source aligns with mass scaling relations on the Fundamental Plane, albeit with a flatter slope indicating sustained coronal-jet coupling.
AI.conclusion: Markarian 590 displays a rare, real-time spectral state transition similar to those in X-ray binaries, confirming scale-invariant accretion processes across black hole masses and demonstrating persistent coronal-jet coupling even during radiatively efficient phases.
